name: cache-tail-policy-subagent-benchmark
description: Synthetic eight-turn normal-subagent conversation for the legacy agent preset. The verifier deterministically pads its stable system prefix to the declared character floor so a live run can observe cache activity without embedding a large, quickly stale role prompt in this fixture.
systemBlocks: You are a focused synthetic investigation subagent. Inspect only the supplied benchmark evidence, return a concise factual result, and keep the tool and output-schema surface unchanged between turns.

turns.user: Inspect the synthetic request builder and identify its TTL input.
turns.assistant: The synthetic builder receives a caller-selected TTL.

turns.user: Identify which synthetic request layer forwards that TTL.
turns.assistant: The outer synthetic request layer forwards the TTL.

turns.user: Describe the synthetic five-minute override precedence.
turns.assistant: The five-minute override wins before the longer-duration policy.

turns.user: Describe the synthetic one-hour eligibility branch.
turns.assistant: The one-hour branch applies to eligible agent-shaped request sources.

turns.user: Check whether the synthetic agent source is a fresh lineage.
turns.assistant: The normal-agent request starts a fresh conversation lineage.

turns.user: Check whether a compatible peer can reuse the stable prefix.
turns.assistant: A compatible peer can reuse matching model, system, tool, and schema prefixes.

turns.user: State the synthetic cold-write risk of the longer TTL.
turns.assistant: A one-shot agent pays a larger cold-write premium without a later reuse.

turns.user: State what the benchmark must report before claiming a win.
turns.assistant: It must report live cache usage and cost deltas; a dry run proves only request validity.
